Module.WhatCanChange.Body: Cooked Blueprints store only the values that differ from their parent class. Those are listed here and can be edited safely in place. Numbers and switches a parent class sets (a Blueprint parent, or the game code for a katana's MaxHealth) are listed as inherited: a change writes them into this asset's own file. Values still not listed come from the game code or another part (projectile, entity setup).

Map.Shape.HandlesHint: Or use the handles in the view. Blue diamonds push it right or left; the blue arrow over each raises or lowers the middle (both up: a hump, one up one down: a wave). Green squares at the ends make it longer or shorter; the green arrow over each raises or lowers that end (a ramp). Made much longer it repeats copy after copy instead of stretching, and an end welds to another piece's end when brought close (Alt: no weld). Red squares at the corners make that side wider or narrower. Other objects get green squares at their ends (longer, shorter) and a red one on top (bigger, smaller).

Map.PickLevel.Body: Select a sublevel or a whole cell (e.g. Cell A_0) in the World tree. Hold the right mouse button to look around and fly with W/A/S/D (Q/E down/up, Shift faster); the wheel sets the speed while you hold it and zooms otherwise; Tab keeps looking without holding (Esc lets go); left-drag an object to move it, wheel while holding it to turn it (Shift = raise, Ctrl = finer), Page Up/Down = raise 1 cm (Shift 10 cm), hold Ctrl to snap, Ctrl+A = all of this kind (Ctrl+Shift+A: whole map). Ctrl+click = add to the selection (Delete, Ctrl+C/V, Extend and dragging then act on all), Shift+click = the whole road or forest, Backspace = last object (again: back). Map.Hole.Title: Hole in the ground
Map.Hole.Caption: For a bunker entrance: players fall through the opening. Experimental: the game draws the hole only on green ground; on amber ground it still draws the ground over it.
Map.Hole.Why: Why only green: the game draws a hole only where the piece of landscape uses a material built with the hole layer in the Unreal editor (about one piece in nine). Each piece's material is compiled for its own set of ground layers; the others have no hole in their compiled shaders, and a mod cannot compile new ones. The collision opens anywhere.

Map.Hole.Warn.Title: Before you cut holes
Map.Hole.Warn.Intro: A hole changes the game's own landscape. What can happen:
Map.Hole.Warn.Update: SCUM updates can change the landscape: export again after every update, because a hole replaces the whole landscape tile (about 760 x 760 m) with your copy.
Map.Hole.Warn.Conflict: Another mod that changes the same landscape tile conflicts with yours: only one of them is used, so its changes or your hole disappear.
Map.Hole.Warn.Server: Players and the server need the same pak (client and server). If they differ, players fall through ground they can see, or stand on air and get pulled back.
Map.Hole.Warn.Ground: Amber places on the Map: the game still draws the ground over the hole. Cover the opening with your own model (a hatch, a bunker entrance).
Map.Hole.Warn.Edge: Green places: the game draws the hole too, but the drawn edge can be up to about 1.5 m off the edge you fall through, as at the game's own bunker entrances. Cover the rim with your own model.
Map.Hole.Warn.Far: From far away a small hole can look closed: the game draws distant ground from smaller copies of its maps.
Map.Hole.Warn.Ai: Zombies, animals and vehicles are not told about the hole: they may walk or drive into it.
Map.Hole.Warn.Backup: Keep a backup of your project (a copy of its folder) before you cut holes.
Map.Hole.Warn.Test: Only the game can confirm a hole: try it on your own server before you share the mod.
Map.Hole.Warn.DontShow: Do not show again for this project

Map.Hole.Warn.Reminder: This project cuts holes in the ground: export again after every SCUM update, install the client and the server pak together, and cover amber holes with your own model.

Spawns.Point.ShowOnMap.Tip: Opens the Map page with the camera on this place and the place selected (its sector loads if it is not shown yet).
Spawns.Point.Spawns.Tip: What this place spawns: its vehicle group, zone settings or biome. A change is saved at once (one undo step).
Spawns.Point.FromZone: A zombie / NPC point spawns what the threat zone around it draws: change the zone's settings to change what comes here.
Spawns.Point.SubZones: Sub-zones (boxes inside the zone with settings of their own, priority in brackets): {0}
Spawns.Point.X.Tip: Where the place stands along the game's X axis, in metres (left to right on the map). Type a value and press Enter or Move here.
Spawns.Point.Y.Tip: Where the place stands along the game's Y axis, in metres (top to bottom on the map). Type a value and press Enter or Move here.
Spawns.Point.Z.Tip: The place's height in metres. A typed height is used as it is; leave it alone and a place moved elsewhere goes onto the ground.
Spawns.Point.Yaw.Tip: Which way the place faces, in degrees (0 = the game's +X, 90 = +Y). A vehicle spawns facing this way.
Spawns.Point.Bad: Type numbers only (a point or a comma for decimals).
Spawns.Point.Apply.Tip: Moves and turns the place to the typed values (one undo step).
Spawns.Point.Ground.Tip: Puts the place on the terrain under it (vehicles 20 cm above it, the others 5 cm), one undo step.
Spawns.Point.NoGround: The terrain here is not known (no island terrain in the game files), so the height stays.
Spawns.Point.Zoom.Tip: Zooms the map in on this place (20 m around it).
Spawns.Point.Delete.Tip: Removes this spawn place from the mod's island data (one undo step; the Delete key on the map does the same).
Spawns.Point.Snap.Tip: When on, a dragged, nudged or typed move puts the place on the terrain where the island's terrain is known. Indoor points always keep their height.
Spawns.Point.Indoor: Indoor point: it stands on a building's floor, so moves keep its height.
Spawns.Point.Keys: On the map: drag to move · arrows 1 m (Shift 10 m, Ctrl 10 cm) · drag the arrow to turn · Q / E turn 15° (Shift 1°) · Delete removes · Ctrl+Z undoes.
Map.SpawnFocus.NotLoaded: Spawn place {0} did not load: turn on Spawns and load its sector.
Spawns.Area.List.Tip: The spawn places of this category inside the area; select one to see its settings, check several to change or remove them together.
Spawns.Area.Check.Tip: Check to change, remove or fix this place together with the other checked ones.
Spawns.Area.CheckAll.Tip: Checks every place in the list, or unchecks them when all are checked.
Spawns.Map.Tip: The island seen from above. Wheel: zoom. Drag: move. The tool above picks a sector, draws an area or places a new spawn.
Spawns.Map.Picture.NotAPicture: {0} is not a PNG or JPG picture.
Spawns.Entries.Title: Settings, presets and biomes
Spawns.Players.FirstSpawn.Title: First spawn of a new character
Spawns.Players.FirstSpawn.Body: SCUM's ServerSettings.ini has no key that chooses where a new character first appears. Whether the game's own spawn data (the first-play game mode and the spawn screen's settings) holds such a place has not been checked yet. If it does not, a rule like 'the first time at place X, then as usual' is server logic, which a mod pak cannot carry. What the server does let you set are the respawn rules below.
Spawns.Players.Respawn.Caption: From the server's ServerSettings.ini (only the keys your file has). Restart the server to use them.
Spawns.S.AllowSector.Tip: Players may pick a sector of the map when they respawn.
Spawns.S.AllowShelter.Tip: Players may respawn at their shelter.
Spawns.S.AllowSquad.Tip: Players may respawn next to a member of their squad.
Spawns.S.RandomPrice.Tip: Fame points a respawn at a random place costs.
Spawns.S.SectorPrice.Tip: Fame points a respawn in a chosen sector costs.
Spawns.S.ShelterPrice.Tip: Fame points a respawn at a shelter costs.
Spawns.S.SquadPrice.Tip: Fame points a respawn at a squadmate costs.
Spawns.S.RandomInitial.Tip: Seconds before this respawn is offered the first time.
Spawns.S.SectorInitial.Tip: Seconds before this respawn is offered the first time.
Spawns.S.ShelterInitial.Tip: Seconds before this respawn is offered the first time.
Spawns.S.SquadInitial.Tip: Seconds before this respawn is offered the first time.
Spawns.S.RandomCooldown.Tip: Seconds before this respawn can be used again.
Spawns.S.SectorCooldown.Tip: Seconds before this respawn can be used again.
Spawns.S.ShelterCooldown.Tip: Seconds before this respawn can be used again.
Spawns.S.SquadCooldown.Tip: Seconds before this respawn can be used again.
Spawns.S.RandomReset.Tip: The server's multiplier for resetting this respawn's cooldown.
Spawns.S.SectorReset.Tip: The server's multiplier for resetting this respawn's cooldown.
Spawns.S.ShelterReset.Tip: The server's multiplier for resetting this respawn's cooldown.
Spawns.S.SquadReset.Tip: The server's multiplier for resetting this respawn's cooldown.
Spawns.NoEditableValues: This entry has no value the page can change.
Spawns.NoNpcGroup: This zone has no armed-NPC group: a zombie weight of 0 turns its spawns off instead of spawning NPCs.
Spawns.NpcWizard.Title: Place NPCs
Spawns.NpcWizard.Hint: Three simple steps: who appears, how many spawn posts, and where on the map. The chance lists and weights are set for you.
Spawns.NpcWizard.Kind.Tip: Which armed NPCs appear. The area gets its own copy of the game's zone settings that spawn only them, so no other place changes.
Spawns.NpcWizard.Posts.Tip: Spawn posts around the point you click, 15 m from it. The NPCs come at some of them, never one on each; how many come is the game's own rule.
Spawns.NpcWizard.Summary: {0} spawn post(s) of {1} around the point you click. In the game, 1 to 3 NPCs come only while a player walks into the area, 30 to 200 m ahead and out of view; then it rests 20 to 30 minutes.
Spawns.NpcWizard.Pick: Pick the place on the map
Spawns.NpcWizard.Pick.Tip: Then click the island map: the NPCs are placed there in one undo step.
Spawns.NpcWizard.Waiting: Click the island map where the NPCs should appear.
Spawns.NpcWizard.Cancel.Tip: Stop picking a place. Nothing is changed.
Spawns.NpcWizard.Done: {0} NPC post(s) of {1} placed. NPCs come only while a player walks in, never one per post.
Spawns.NpcWizard.NoTypes: The game's NPC kinds could not be read.
Spawns.NpcWizard.OwnCopy: Own copy of one NPC (the others stay as they are)
Spawns.NpcWizard.OwnCopy.Tip: Copies the whole chain of the chosen NPC under new names: zone settings, encounter, preset, character and its data. Nothing else that uses the stock ones changes. The copy ships with the Spawns pak.
Spawns.NpcWizard.Character.Tip: Which NPC of this kind to copy.
Spawns.NpcWizard.OwnSummary: {0} spawn post(s) of your own copy of {1} around the point you click. The stock NPCs and their data stay as the game has them. In the game, 1 to 3 NPCs come only while a player walks into the area, 30 to 200 m ahead and out of view; then it rests 20 to 30 minutes.
Spawns.NpcWizard.DoneOwn: {0} NPC post(s) of your own copy of {1} placed. The stock NPCs are untouched. NPCs come only while a player walks in, never one per post.
Spawns.AllWeightsZero: Every weight of this list is 0: the zone spawns nothing.
Spawns.OutOfDate: The project changed since this page read the values (another page, undo or redo). The page now shows the current values: make the change again and save.
Spawns.PartsDefault: {0} more parts use the game's default chance (not stored in the preset).
Spawns.OutOfRange.Tip: The game or your project stores a value outside the usual range; the slider was widened to hold it.
Map.Spawns.Tip: Shows the game's spawn places as pins (Colours explains each colour and turns each kind on or off). Click a pin to see what can spawn there.
Spawn.Loot: Loot spawner: {0} loot points (gold pins), what spawns there: {1}. Move it and all its points move.
Spawn.Building: {0} loot points inside (small gold pins): {1}. They are part of the building and move with it.
Spawn.LootZone: Loot zone: not a spawn place; the loot spawners inside it get a different chance or kind of loot.
Spawn.Sentry: Sentry spawner: a sentry stands here and patrols {0} points (pink pins).
Spawn.Creature: Bunker creature spawn point (Razor, kill box).
Spawn.PlayerDrop: Drop zone: where players can drop in during events.
Spawn.CarShop: Car shop: {0} places where bought vehicles appear (blue pins).
Paint.Title: Paint
Paint.Caption: The body paint of this vehicle. Pick a colour or a finish: the model shows it at once, shine included. Ctrl+Z steps back.
Paint.Colour.Tip: The paint colour. Click to pick any colour.
Paint.Second.Tip: The second colour of a two-tone body.
Paint.Finish.Original.Tip: Back to the game's own paint.
Paint.Finish.Tip: Applies this finish: the colour, and metal and clear coat where the paint has them.
Paint.Metal.Tip: How metallic the paint is (100 % = like gold or chrome).
Paint.ClearCoat.Tip: How glossy the varnish over the paint is.
Paint.Note: Every vehicle of this model in the game gets this paint. It goes into the mod with Export mod; players need the client pak to see it.
Paint.Apply.Tip: Records the paint in your project; Export mod writes it into the pak.
Paint.Discard.Tip: Back to the last applied paint.
Paint.AppliedDetail: {0} paint value(s) recorded in the project.
Paint.Together.Tip: On: a colour or finish picked for one part goes to every part (body, doors, armour), so the whole vehicle matches.
Paint.Armour.Tip: Fits an armour kit in the 3D view so you can see it and paint it with the vehicle.
Paint.Added: Has no paint of its own: the mod adds it (colour, shine and a full colour mask). Every vehicle whose armour uses this material gets it.
Paint.Plain: Plain finish (an even colour, no scrap-metal print)
Paint.Plain.Tip: On: the part's printed texture (rust, signs, patches) is swapped for the game's flat white one, so the paint is one even colour; the plates keep their shape. Off: the paint goes over the printed texture.
Map.Parts.Tip: On (default): a click on a building picks only the part under the cursor (the shell, a door, a shelf, a lamp) to move, copy or delete it alone; Ctrl+click adds more parts; Shift+click takes the whole building. Off: a click takes the whole building, Alt+click picks one part.
Map.Part.Of: {0} of {1} (only this building changes; Shift+click takes the whole building)
Spawn.VehiclePlace: World vehicle spawn point, group {0}: a car, bike, boat or plane of this group can appear here. Move, copy or delete it to change where vehicles spawn (written into the server and client paks).
Spawn.Zombie: Zombie / NPC spawn point ({0}): the threat zone around it spawns its characters here. Move, copy or delete it.
Spawn.Zone: Threat zone {0}, {1} × {2} m from the centre: its zombies and NPCs spawn inside. Move it; Scale makes it bigger or smaller.
Spawn.Animal: Hunting area ({0}), radius {1} m: animals of this kind live here. Move it; Scale changes its size.
Update.UpToDate.Tip: You have the newest version ({0}). Click to check GitHub again; the app also checks every 30 minutes.
Update.Offline.Tip: GitHub could not be reached. Click to try again.
Map.Part.Whole.Tip: Select the building this part belongs to, with everything in it (Shift+click on the building does the same)
Map.SpawnLegend.Tip: What each pin colour means; switch each kind of spawn place on or off
Map.SpawnLegend.Title: Spawn places on the map
Map.SpawnLegend.Hint: Each colour is one kind of spawn place. Untick a kind to hide it. Click a pin on the map to see what spawns there.
Spawn.Layer.Loot.Tip: Where items appear (shelves, crates, piles). Click one to see every item that can spawn there and how rare it is.
Spawn.Layer.Vehicles.Tip: Where cars, bikes, boats and planes appear. Click one to see which vehicles can spawn there.
Spawn.Layer.Zombies.Tip: Where the zombies and NPCs of the threat zone around them appear.
Spawn.Layer.Zones.Tip: A circle with a pin in the middle: the area of a threat zone; its zombies spawn inside it. The circle is the size of the zone.
Spawn.Layer.Animals.Tip: A circle with a pin in the middle: animals of that kind live inside it.
Spawn.Layer.LootZones.Tip: Not a spawn place: they change the chance or kind of loot of the loot points inside them.
Spawn.Layer.Sentries.Tip: The pin is where a sentry stands; pink pins are the points it patrols.
Spawn.Layer.Creatures.Tip: Razors and kill box creatures inside bunkers.
Spawn.Layer.CarShops.Tip: Where a trader puts the vehicles players buy.
Spawn.Layer.Drops.Tip: Where players can drop in during events.
Map.Loot.Title: Loot
Map.Loot.Lootable.Tip: Off: decoration only. Nobody can search it and it holds no loot. On: players search it for the loot of the presets below. Many objects carry loot in their model too (a locker's, a crate's): when you change it, the export gives the object a copy of its model without that loot, so in game it gives only what is listed here.
Map.Grass.Title: Grass
Map.Grass.Clear: Clear grass and spawns under it
Map.Grass.Clear.Tip: On: the exported mod removes the landscape grass under this object's outline, so no grass grows through it (bushes and trees stay as the game has them), and the vehicle and zombie/NPC spawn points inside it, so nothing spawns in it. Off: leave both as they are.
Map.Loot.Presets.Tip: The loot presets a search of it draws from: its own, or its model's when it has none of its own. Their groups and items are listed under "What can spawn here".
Map.Loot.Pick.Tip: Pick a loot preset to add (the game's Examine presets).
Map.Loot.PickFirst: Pick a loot preset first, then tick Lootable.
Map.NoLoot.Tip: On: the exported mod takes all loot out of this placed object: its searchable parts (desks, cabinets, crates, also the lockers it carries) give nothing and its loot points on shelves and floors are taken out. Parts whose model carries loot draw a copy of the model without it (it looks the same). Item spawners, and items already lying in a save, stay. Off: the loot the game gives the original.
Map.NoLoot.On: No loot inside is on for this object: the export takes its loot out, so its presets cannot be changed here.
Map.AddObject.NoLoot.Tip: On: objects you add, paste or copy from now on get "No loot inside" (each one can be switched in the Map's properties). Placed item spawners are left as they are.
SpawnInfo.Title: What can spawn here
SpawnInfo.Hint: Read from the game files. Rarity: Common appears most often, Extremely rare almost never.
SpawnInfo.VehicleGroup.Tip: One of these vehicles can appear on this point (the server's vehicle limits decide how many there are on the map).
SpawnInfo.NoVehicles: No vehicle of the game uses this group.
SpawnInfo.NoPreset: This preset could not be read from the game files.
SpawnInfo.Chance: {0} % chance that something spawns, {1} item(s) each time
Map.LootPoint.Of: Point {0} of {1} in {2}: part of the building, it moves with it (Shift+click takes the building).
Map.SpawnPoint.Of: Point {0} of {1} of {2}: drag it with the gizmo, Duplicate adds a point beside it, Delete removes it (Shift+click takes the spawner).
Paint.Caption.Weapon: The colour of this weapon. Pick a colour or a finish: the model shows it at once, shine included. Ctrl+Z steps back.
Paint.Note.Weapon: Every weapon of this model in the game gets this colour (each part here is one material; a magazine or attachment that shares it changes too). It goes into the mod with Export mod; players need the client pak to see it.
Paint.Tint: The game tints this weapon's own texture: the mod adds the colour and the metal. Left alone it stays as the game has it.
Paint.Even: Even colour (no wood or metal print)
Paint.Even.Tip: On: the weapon's printed texture (wood grain, worn metal) is swapped for the game's flat white one, so the colour is one even coat; shape, wear and shine stay. Off: the colour tints the weapon's own texture.
Paint.AllOriginal.Tip: Every part back to the paint the game has (Apply paint records it; Ctrl+Z steps back).
Paint.Note.Clone: Only this clone gets this paint ({0}); the original keeps its own. It goes into the mod with Export mod; players need the client pak to see it.
Paint.CloneShared: This clone was made before clones had their own paint, so painting it would paint the original too. Remove it and clone again to paint it on its own.
Map.Brush.Tip: Brush select: hold the left mouse button and move over the map; everything inside the yellow circle is added to the selection. Turn it off and the selection stays: Ctrl+click what you want to keep, then Delete removes the rest.
Map.Brush.Size.Tip: Size of the brush circle (radius in metres).
Map.Shape.NoBendBuilding: Houses and other wide objects do not bend like bridges and roads. On a slope use Fit to ground; tilt and turn them with the sliders below.
Map.Shape.NoBendRock: Rocks and cliffs do not bend: the game's collision fits only the straight rock (bent, players would sink into it and fall under it). Tilt and turn it with the sliders below.
Map.Shape.TiltFront.Tip: Leans the object towards its front or back, up to 90° either way (like standing it on a slope).
Map.Shape.TiltSide.Tip: Leans the object to its left or right, up to 90° either way.
Map.Shape.Turn.Tip: Turns the object around, which way it faces (degrees).
Module.Part.Damage.Tip: The melee weapon's row in the game's weapon table (WeaponDesc_Table): damage per hit, stamina, cutting and stabbing. A clone gets a row of its own, starting from its template's values.
Module.Group.Thrown: When thrown, not the hit damage (see Hit damage) · {0}
Module.Inherited.Tip: This file does not store this value: it takes it from its parent class {0}. A change is written into this item's own file; the parent and the other items keep theirs.
Module.Inherited.GameDefault.Tip: Set in the game's code, not in its files, so the studio cannot show it. Leave the box empty to keep the game's value.
Module.Part.Engine.Tip: The engine's torque curve: how hard it pulls at each rpm. Higher torque = faster acceleration and a higher top speed (a clone has its own copy, the stock vehicle stays).
Module.Note.Airplane: A plane flies on its propeller. Propeller force is how hard it pulls (180000 in the game's code; the plane's file does not store it, a change writes it there). Max velocity is the speed it cannot pass, in cm/s (8332.5 = 300 km/h; km/h × 27.78). To fly faster, raise Propeller force, and Max velocity too to go above 300 km/h: Max velocity alone does not make it pull harder. Its engine, gear and wheel values (Key stats off) only roll it on the ground: none of its wheels is driven.
Module.Note.AirplaneEngine: This engine part sets how the plane's engine revs and sounds, not how hard the plane pulls: that is Propeller force, in the plane's own values (the first part in the list).
Module.Note.Container: What it holds: Num rows × Num columns cells (each at most 255), and at most Max contained weight kg while Has contained weight limit is on. A value marked inherited comes from its parent or the game's code (1 × 1 cells, 10 kg); a change writes it into this item. Grid inventory row span and column span are the room the item itself takes.
Module.CannotBuildClone: The studio cannot build this clone, so the pak would not have it: {0}
Module.Part.Parts.Tip: Which part every slot of the vehicle spawns with in the spawn preset {0}. ManualSpawn is used by #SpawnVehicle, AutomaticSpawn by vehicles found in the world, Purchase by the traders. Pick another part that fits the slot, or No part.
Module.Part.Attachments.Tip: Which attachments and magazines each socket of the weapon takes, by mount type. Tick a type to allow it, untick it to take it away.
Module.ShowOnCar.Tip: Show this part highlighted on the vehicle in the 3D view
Map.FarModel: That is a far-view model, not a building
Map.FarModelDetail: {0} is the game's far-away picture of a place: low detail, one blurred texture, no collision, and it includes whatever stands around it (cars, walls). To place a real building, select it on the map (Shift+click takes the whole building), copy it with Ctrl+C and paste it with Ctrl+V where you want it.
Map.Underside: That is the underside of the water, not the lake
Map.UndersideDetail: {0} is the inside-out underside of a lake (flipped normals, underwater material): the game draws it only from under the water, so placed as an object it never shows. Place {1} instead.
Map.Underside.TopSurface: the lake's top surface (the same mesh without _FN)
Map.State.HiddenInGame: never shows in the game (the underside of the water): delete it and place the lake's top surface
Map.HiddenInGame.Tip: Never shows in the game: the underside of the water (flipped normals, underwater material).
Spawn.Layer.Traders.Tip: Outpost traders (armorer, mechanic, doctor, barber …): the pin stands where the NPC does. Select it to move, copy or delete the trader with its counter.
Spawn.Trader: Trade post: {0}. NPC: {1}. Move, copy (Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V) or delete it like any object; the server's EconomyOverride.json lists traders by these names.
Module.Part.Trade.Tip: How the traders sell it (the game's tradeable table): purchase and sale price, fame points needed, whether players can buy or sell it. A clone is sold by the same trader as its original, under its own name.
Mods.Title: Imported mods
Mods.Caption: Someone else's pak mod (a map, a landscape, cars): the app reads it over the game, you edit on top of it, and Export mod puts it into your pak with your changes.
Mods.Import.Tip: Pick a .pak mod. It is unpacked into this project's mods folder; the map, vehicles and assets then show it.
Mods.Remove.Tip: Takes the mod out of this project (your own edits stay in the history).
Mods.ImportedDetail: {0}: {1:N0} files. The game files are read again with the mod on top.
Mods.NeedProject: Open or create a project first: an imported mod belongs to a project.
Map.Ground.Tip: Lays the selected building (or every object of the multi-selection) on the slope under it: tilted the way the ground runs, its bottom on the ground, facing the same way. Ctrl+Z undoes it.
Map.Ground.DropTip: Drop to the surface: sets the selection down on whatever is right under it (ground, road, roof, wall, a vehicle) without sinking in. Buildings follow the slope, trees stay upright. Key: End. Ctrl+Z undoes it.
Map.Ground.NoGround: No ground under it: load the landscape tiles around it (or the whole island) first.
Map.Ground.LootPointFixed: This loot point comes with the building's class: it moves with the building and cannot be set down on its own (Shift+click takes the building).
Map.Landscape.Tip: The whole island: other trees in place of the game's, and laying objects on the ground.
Map.NotDrawn.Title: Not drawn as in the game
Map.NotDrawn.Caption: Ground grass: the game scatters short grass and flowers over the meadows from its ground layers; the studio does not draw them, so meadows look bare here. They are there in the game and your edits leave them as they are (except Clear grass under an object you place). Objects in plain light grey: the studio could not read their colour from the game's material; the game draws them in colour.
Map.Looks.Title: Ground look
Map.Looks.Caption: Changes the ground of the whole island in your mod: soft ground and the grass on it. Roads, rocks, rivers and the sea floor stay. Far away the ground keeps the game's colour.
Map.Looks.InGame: The whole island, in the client and server paks; it shows in the game after Export mod
Map.Looks.NeedProject: Open or create a project first: the ground look is an edit of the project.
Map.Trees.Title: Trees
Map.Trees.Caption: Draws another tree everywhere the game has one (its look and its collision), on the whole island.
Map.Trees.Swap.Tip: Every tree of the first kind on the island becomes the second kind in your mod.
Map.Trees.PutBack.Tip: Draws the game's own tree again.
Mods.Carry.Tip: On: Export mod puts this mod into your pak. Off: it stays its own pak (install it on the server and for players yourself, for a big map); your pak loads after it, so your edits still win.
Map.SpawnPart.Note: A spawn place of this building: drag it, or type a new location and Apply transform. Copy, Duplicate and Delete are off for it: it has no mesh of its own, and what the game does with a removed spawner is not known.
Map.BlueprintNotPlaced: This Blueprint is not on the island
Map.BlueprintNotPlacedDetail: '{0}' is not placed anywhere on the island, so there is nothing to copy. Only Blueprints the game placed in a level (and items) can be added.
Support.Button.Tip: Support the developer, or report a problem, an idea or a question (it reaches the developer in English, whatever language you write).
Support.Title: Support
Support.Subtitle: Made by one person in their spare time. A coffee helps; a report helps too.
Support.Donate.Title: Support the developer
Support.Donate.Text: If the app saves you time, you can send something by PayPal. Questions and business: the e-mail.
Support.PayPal.Tip: Opens the developer's PayPal page in your browser.
Support.Report.Title: Report a problem
Support.Report.Text: Write in your own language: it is translated to English and lands on the developer's Discord, with the app's version. One report a minute.
Support.Report.Category.Tip: What this is: something broken, a wish, or a question.
Support.Report.Question: A question
Support.Report.Watermark: What happened, where (which level or object), and what you expected…
Support.Report.Box.Tip: Your report, in any language. Say what you did, what happened and what you expected; the level or object name helps.
Support.Report.Details: Add version, language, system and the last log lines
Support.Report.Details.Tip: Sends the app's version, your UI language, your Windows version and the last 12 lines of the app's log with the report (no files, no paths of yours).
Support.Report.Send.Tip: Translates the report to English and sends it to the developer's Discord.
Support.Report.SentAsWritten: Sent as written (the translation service could not be reached). Thank you!
Support.Report.Unavailable: This build cannot send reports (it was built without the developer's address). Report on GitHub instead:
Support.Report.Issues.Tip: Opens the project's issue tracker in your browser.
Map.LocalAxes.Tip: On: the gizmo's arrows follow the selected object's own front, side and up. Off: the world's north, east and up. The turn ring stays level either way.
Map.Axes.Tip: Which way the gizmo points, as in Blender: Global = the world's north, east and up; Local = the selected object's own front, side and up (best for objects already turned); View = the screen's right, up and towards you. The comma key switches it.
Spawn.Layer.Effects.Tip: Lights, fires, smoke, sounds and fog: actors with nothing to draw but an effect. The pin selects the actor; delete or move it like any object.
Spawn.Layer.Markers.Tip: Other actors with no model of their own: NPCs, quest markers, triggers, helpers. The pin selects the actor; delete or move it like any object.
Spawn.Effect: An effect ({0}: {1}): nothing to draw, so a pin stands for it. Delete or move it like any object.
Spawn.Marker: An actor with no model ({0}: {1}): a pin stands for it. Delete or move it like any object.
Discord.Button.Tip: Opens the community's Discord server in your browser: help, mods, bug reports and release news.
Share.Button.Tip: Share your map edits with other players, or get theirs from the gallery.
Share.Title: Share your mod
Share.Subtitle: Only your project's own edits travel: never game files or paks.
Share.Close.Tip: Closes this card; what you typed stays here until you share it.
Share.Tab.Share.Tip: Upload your project's edits with a picture and a description.

Map.Prefabs.Export.Title: Export prefab
Map.Prefabs.Import.Title: Import prefab

Map.Prefabs.Skipped: {0} object(s) skipped, no longer in the game files: {1}

Settings.Prefabs.Import.Tip: Add a .ssprefab file to your library
Settings.Toolbar.Tip: Choose which items the Map header shows
Settings.Toolbar.Hint: Switch off what you never use; the header makes room for the rest. The settings button at the end of the Map header has the same switches.
History.GoTo.Tip: Fly the camera to the object this edit changed and select it
History.Select.Tip: Select the object this edit changed, without moving the camera
History.NoPlace: This edit has no place on the map (it changes the whole island or a package).
History.NotInMap: {0} is not in the map now (its level is not loaded, or the edit was undone).
Map.Trees.ReplaceHint: This swaps a tree type on the whole island. To change only the selected object:
Map.Brush.Select.Tip: Brush selects: everything the circle passes over is added to the selection.
Map.Brush.Paint.Tip: Brush plants: hold the left mouse button and sweep; the palette's objects are scattered inside the circle, spaced apart and standing on the ground. Letting go is one undo step.
Map.Paint.Palette.Tip: What the brush plants: trees, bushes, rocks or any object, and how far apart
Map.Paint.Title: Paint objects
Map.Paint.Caption: Hold the left mouse button and sweep the circle over the ground: these objects are planted evenly inside it, never closer than the spacing to each other or to what already stands there, and never on roads, paths, runways, water or rocks.
Map.Paint.Empty: Nothing to plant yet: pick trees, bushes or rocks in the card on the left (select an object on the map first to get its family too).
Map.Paint.Remove.Tip: Take it out of the palette
Map.Paint.Spacing.Tip: Smallest distance between two planted objects, in metres; the second slider sets the largest (the game's forests: about 3–4 m).
Map.Paint.SpacingMax.Tip: Largest distance between two planted objects, in metres; each one keeps its own random distance between the two sliders (1–3 m by default).
Map.Paint.Timer.Tip: Plant on a timer: while you hold the button, one object is planted every interval at the free spot nearest the centre of the circle, whether you move or not. The spacing and the ground rules still apply; when the circle is full, move the brush.
Map.Paint.Every.Tip: Seconds between two planted objects in timer mode.
Map.Paint.RandomSize.Tip: Each plant comes 0.9 to 1.15 times its size; buildings stay as they are
Map.Paint.RandomTurn.Tip: Each object is turned at random about its upright axis
Map.Paint.Note: Trees, bushes and rocks that the landscape tile under the brush already has as foliage become new trees of that foliage, chopped and collided like the game's own. Anything else is placed as a new object.
Map.Paint.OnObjects.Tip: Also plant on roofs, floors and other objects under the circle. Off: only on bare ground. Roads, paths, runways, water and rocks are always left out.
Map.Paint.Skipped.NoGround: {0} with no ground loaded under them
Map.Paint.Full: The circle is full at this spacing: move the brush to plant more.
Map.Paint.Marks: Too many spots to mark them all: a click here plants {0} and leaves out {1}.

Page.economy.Title: Economy
Page.economy.Subtitle: Traders, prices and stock: the server's EconomyOverride.json
Map.Trader.Title: Trader
Map.Trader.Hint: A copy of the game's trade post of this type, where the camera aims. Its name is its section in the server's economy.
Map.Trader.Type.Tip: Which trader: armory, general goods, mechanic, doctor, bartender, barber, harbourmaster, hunters or the bank.
Map.Trader.Name: Name
Map.Trader.Name.Tip: The trader's name in the economy (letters, digits and _), e.g. A_3_Armory. Its prices are set on the Economy page under this name.
Map.Trader.Outpost.Tip: Outpost_A_0, Outpost_B_4, Outpost_C_2 or Outpost_Z_3 joins that outpost; another name (Outpost_A_3) makes a new outpost here.
Map.Trader.Place.Tip: Adds the trader in front of the camera as one step of the history (undo removes it).
Map.Trader.BadNameDetail: Use letters, digits and _ only (for example A_3_Armory and Outpost_A_3).
Map.Trader.NoSource: No trade post of that type
Map.Trader.NoSourceDetail: The game's outposts have no {0} trade post to copy.
Map.Trader.NameTakenDetail: A trader named {0} exists already; each trader needs its own name (it is its economy section).
Map.Trader.NotATraderDetail: {0} is no trader of the game's outposts, so there is no trade post to place it with.
Economy.PlaceTrader.Tip: Puts a trader of this type on the Map where its camera looks (fly there first). It gets the cell's name and outpost and its section here with the game's stock.
Economy.PlaceTrader.Caption: The trader goes where the Map's camera is looking: fly there first, then pick the type. Move it with the gizmo afterwards.
Map.Lift.Title: Lift
Map.Lift.Hint: A copy of the mechanic's car or bike lift, where the camera aims, tied to the mechanic you pick (it goes into that mechanic's level).
Map.Lift.Kind.Tip: Which lift: the car lift or the bike lift of the game's mechanics.
Map.Lift.Mechanic.Tip: The mechanic whose menu repairs and upgrades the vehicle on this lift: a stock mechanic of a loaded level or a Mechanic trader you placed; nearest to the camera first.
Map.Lift.Place.Tip: Adds the lift in front of the camera, in the mechanic's level, as one step of the history (undo removes it).
Map.Lift.NoMechanicDetail: Load a level with a mechanic (the B_4 outpost) or place a Mechanic trader first: a lift must stand in its mechanic's level.
Map.Lift.NoSourceDetail: The game's outposts have no {0} to copy.
Map.EditStock.Tip: Opens this trader on the Economy page: what it sells, prices and fame needed.
Economy.ExportedDetail: {0}. It replaces the server's own EconomyOverride.json (SCUM\Saved\Config\WindowsServer): import the server's file first, so its own changes are kept.
Economy.BadFile: The project's EconomyOverride.json could not be read
Economy.NoProject: No project open: nothing here can be changed or kept. Open or create a project to edit the economy.
Economy.Export.Tip: Writes EconomyOverride.json into the export folder (Server and Client), next to the mod paks.
Economy.Empty.Body: Connect the game's files: the traders and what they sell come from them.
Economy.Search.Tip: Shows the items whose name or code contains this text.
Economy.Category.Tip: Shows one trade category; the buttons next to it act on what is shown.
Economy.PricesUp.Tip: Raises the price and sale price of every item shown by 10 %.
Economy.PricesDown.Tip: Lowers the price and sale price of every item shown by 10 %.
Economy.OffSale.Tip: The trader stops selling every item shown (pick a category first to disable just that category).
Economy.OnSale.Tip: The trader sells every item shown.
Economy.ResetTrader.Tip: Back to the game's prices and stock for this trader.
Economy.Sell.Tip: What a player gets for selling one.
Economy.Fame.Tip: Fame points needed to buy it.
Economy.AfterSaleBox.Tip: Sold only after a player has sold one to the trader.
Economy.Note: Rows marked as changed are written to EconomyOverride.json; items with the "added" badge are written in full. Everything else stays as the game has it. "locked" items cannot be changed by a server; items "not in your game files" keep the file's own values.
Economy.ReadyDetail: {0} is ready: its section lists the {1} items of its stock at the game's prices (Economy page).
Economy.AddItems.Tip: Opens the list of every item of the game: tick the ones this trader should sell too.
Economy.AddSearch.Tip: Shows the items whose name, code or category contains this text.
Economy.AddChecked.Tip: Adds the ticked items to this trader at the game's prices; change them afterwards in the list.
Economy.AddNote: An added item is written in full (price, sale price, fame) with can-be-purchased true, so the server sells it at this trader too.
Economy.Remove.Tip: Removes the item: an added one leaves the trader, one of its own stock goes off sale (a server can only stop selling it).
Economy.PutBack.Tip: Puts the item back on sale.
Economy.View.Tip: Numbers: the traders and their items with pictures and prices. Code: the same economy as the EconomyOverride.json text the export writes, to read, edit or paste a whole file.
Economy.Code.Tip: The project's EconomyOverride.json exactly as the export writes it. Edit or paste: once it reads without errors it is applied as one step (Ctrl+Z outside this box undoes it).
Economy.Code.Draft: Not applied: {0} errors. Your text is kept; the numbers show the last valid economy.
Economy.Code.Format.Tip: Applies the text and writes it the way the game writes the file (tabs, one value per line).
Economy.Code.Discard.Tip: Throws away the text that was not applied and shows the project's economy again.
Economy.Code.Problem.Tip: Click to put the cursor where the problem is.
Economy.Code.Scope.Tip: Settings + one trader: the file's settings and the section of the trader picked next to it, fast to type in. Whole file: every section at once (slow to type in when placed traders list their whole stock). Either way the export writes the whole file.
Economy.Problem.Syntax: This is not valid JSON here (a missing comma, quote or bracket?).
Economy.Problem.NoRoot: The file has no "economy-override" object at the top.
Economy.Problem.NotAnObject: {2} does not hold what the game expects here (an object or a list).
Economy.Problem.MissingCode: An entry of {0} has no tradeable-code: the server skips it.
Economy.Problem.BadBool: {2} is not true, false or default: "{3}".
Economy.Problem.DuplicateKey: {2} is written twice here; the game reads only one of them.
Economy.Problem.DuplicateEntry: {1} is listed twice at {0}; only one entry can stay.
Economy.Problem.UnknownTrader: {0} is neither a trader of the game nor one placed on the map: the server uses the section only where a trader of that name exists.
Economy.Problem.UnknownCode: {1} is not in your game files (a mod's item or a typo?).
Economy.Problem.ImmuneCode: {1} is locked: the game does not let a server change it, so this entry does nothing.
Economy.Problem.HiddenTrader: {0}'s trade post is deleted in this project: its section is kept but not exported.
Economy.Problem.UnknownKey: {2} is not a key the game writes; it is kept as written.
Economy.Problem.SellAboveBuy: {1} at {0} sells for more than it costs: players can buy and sell it for profit.
Economy.Problem.NegativeValue: {2} is {3}: below -1 means nothing; -1 keeps the game's value.
Economy.Import.Tip: Reads an EconomyOverride.json (your server's live file, or an older list) into the project: it becomes the project's economy, in both views. Values left at -1 or default stay that way. Ctrl+Z undoes it.
Economy.Import.Title: Import an EconomyOverride.json
Economy.Import.RefusedDetail: {0} has {1} errors; nothing was changed. Its text is open in Code with the problems listed.
Economy.Import.NotBackedUp: {0} was not imported: the project's EconomyOverride.json could not be backed up first. Nothing was changed.
Economy.Import.DraftKept: {0} has {1} errors; nothing was changed. Your own text in Code is not applied yet: apply or discard it, then import again to fix the file there.
Economy.Settings.Tip: The file's economy-override settings: restock, rotation, price rules and gold. Each one has its own Reset to the game's value.
Economy.Setting.Unknown.Tip: A key the game does not write; it is kept as written.
Economy.Setting.economy-reset-time-hours: Hours between resets of the whole economy; -1 = never.
Economy.Setting.prices-randomization-tim: Hours between random price changes; -1 = never.
Economy.Setting.tradeable-rotation-time-: Shortest time, in game hours, before the traders rotate the items they offer.
Longest time, in game hours, before the traders rotate the items they offer.
Earliest game hour of the day a rotation happens.
Latest game hour of the day a rotation happens.
Economy.Setting.fully-restock-tradeable-: Hours a trader takes to restock an item fully.
Economy.Setting.trader-funds-change-rate: How fast the traders' money refills (1 = the game's rate).
1: prices move with what players buy and sell (delta-price); 0: prices stay fixed.
Economy.Setting.prices-subject-to-player: 1: prices follow how many players are online; 0: they do not.
Economy.Setting.gold-price-subject-to-gl: 1: the gold price follows the server's price multiplier; 0: it does not.
Economy.Setting.gold-base-price.Tip: Base price of gold; -1 = the game's.
Economy.Setting.gold-sale-price-modifier: What a trader pays for gold, as a share of its price; -1 = the game's.
Economy.Setting.gold-price-change-percen: Percentage the gold price moves per step; -1 = the game's.
Economy.Setting.gold-price-change-per-st: Amount the gold price moves per step; -1 = the game's.
Economy.Setting.economy-logging.Tip: 1: the server writes the economy's events to its log; 0: it does not.
1: traders never run out of money.
1: traders never run out of items. Stock is server-wide: the file has no stock per trader or per item.
Economy.Setting.global-only-after-player: 1: every item is sold only after a player has sold one to a trader.
Economy.Setting.tradeable-rotation-enabl: 1: traders rotate the items they offer; 0: they offer everything all the time.
Economy.Setting.enable-fame-point-requir: 1: buying needs the item's required-famepoints; 0: no fame needed.
Economy.Delta.Tip: delta-price: how far the price moves when players buy and sell it. Empty or -1 = the game's.
Economy.Badge.Unknown.Tip: Your game files do not know this code (a mod's item or a typo): the file's values are kept as they are and the buttons above leave it alone.
Economy.UnknownTrader.Tip: A section of the file for a trader that is neither the game's nor placed on the map: the server uses it only where a trader of that name exists.
Economy.Value.Invalid: Not a number: {0}. Digits only; empty or -1 = the game's value.
Economy.ResetTraderDoneDetail: {0} is back to the game's stock. Ctrl+Z undoes it.
Economy.ChangedOutsideDetail: Another program changed the project's EconomyOverride.json. That version was kept as {0} and replaced by the project's economy; use Import to bring it in.
Economy.TablesFailed: The game's economy could not be read
Economy.TablesFailedDetail: The traders and their stock come from the game files: {0}
Economy.Retry.Tip: Reads the game's economy tables again.
Nav.craftables.Tip: Make any object craftable: players craft it and place it like the game's furniture (the Craftables mod).
Page.craftables.Title: Craftables
Page.craftables.Subtitle: Any object as a craftable players place, with its recipe: the Craftables mod
Craftables.NoProject: Open a project to keep craftables
Craftables.NoMesh: {0} shows no static mesh: it cannot become a craftable.
Craftables.Undo.Tip: Step back the last change of the craftables list.
Craftables.Empty.Body: Connect the game files to pick objects and see their 3D pictures.
Craftables.Add.Watermark: Add: search a mesh or Blueprint…
Craftables.Add.Tip: Type part of a name: static meshes and Blueprints that do not move on their own (no characters, animals or vehicles).
Craftables.AddOne.Tip: Add this object to the craftables with a suggested recipe.
Craftables.Note: Export mod builds them as their own pak (Craftables mod) with the project's pak.
Craftables.Recipe.Tip: Edit the selected craftable: its name, kind and recipe.
Craftables.Gallery.Tip: Every object and inventory item of the game (and of mods the app reads) in 3D pictures, by category: click one to make it craftable.
Craftables.Gallery.Hint: Click a picture to make it craftable and edit its recipe; added ones open their recipe.
Craftables.Gallery.Other: Mods, DLC packs and newer files
Craftables.Name: Name in game
Craftables.Name.Tip: The recipe's and the object's name in game. Its asset name is fixed the first time it is saved, so renaming it later keeps what players already built.
Craftables.TokenTaken: {0} already uses the asset name {1}: this craftable would be left out of the export. Rename it to give it an asset name of its own.
Craftables.Kind.Tip: Furniture: placed like the game's furniture. Station: other recipes can need it nearby. Power: gives electricity in a radius.
Craftables.Picture.Tip: The picture the crafting menu shows for it: type part of a game picture's name (ICO_...) and pick one. Empty = its own picture (an item's inventory icon, a game element's recipe picture); a mesh the game has no picture of gets one drawn from its 3D model at export.
Craftables.Picture.Reset.Tip: Shows its own picture again (an item's inventory icon or a game element's recipe picture; drawn from its 3D model when the game has none).
Craftables.Picture.Model.Tip: Shows a picture drawn from its 3D model at export, like the game's icons: the object alone on a transparent background, seen from the front left. Use it when its own picture is not the right one.
Craftables.Picture.Import.Tip: Uses a PNG or JPG of yours as its picture in the crafting menu: it is copied into the project's icons folder and fitted to the game's icon size at export (transparent areas stay transparent).
Craftables.Picture.Import.Title: Choose its picture
Craftables.Picture.FromModel: Picture: drawn from its 3D model at export.
Craftables.Picture.Unreadable: {0} is not a picture the studio can read (PNG or JPG).
Craftables.ShowsIn.Tip: The section of the game's crafting menu where this recipe appears. Only the game's own sections exist: a new section name needs the game's tag list and menu, which a mod cannot add.
Craftables.MadeIn.Building.Tip: Placed in the world and built with resources, like base building: the recipe is in the building menu.
Craftables.MadeIn.Crafting.Tip: Crafted into the inventory, like the game's items (a power object is such an item, placed afterwards). A 3D model cannot become a new inventory item yet: only items of the game are Items.
Craftables.Material.Tip: Main material: picks the suggested ingredients (wood, metal, brick, cement, stone, fabric).
Craftables.ItemNote: An item of the game: the new recipe makes it. The crafting menu shows the item's own name and icon, in the section of its kind (weapons, ammunition, clothes, tools…).
Craftables.Station.Tip: A station craftable of this project the player must stand next to (its item carries a tool tag the recipe asks for).
Craftables.NeedsPower.Tip: Kept in the project; the game's data has no such switch, so the export reports it (native code).
Craftables.Radius.Tip: The green circle: objects inside it get electricity (game generator 10 m, small one 5 m).
Craftables.Output.Tip: Electricity it gives (game generator 500, small one 250).
Craftables.Fuel.Tip: Fuel use (game generator 0.13889); 0 = it never needs fuel.
Craftables.DayOnly.Tip: Kept in the project; the generator's data has no day/night switch, so the export reports it (native code).
Craftables.Suggest.Tip: The recipe from the material and size, scaled from the game's own base-building recipes.
Craftables.Tag.Tip: The game's ingredient tag (CI_Plank, CI_Nails, CI_Group_Toolbox …); any CI_ tag of the game can be typed.
Craftables.Amount.Tip: Amount without skill; skilled players need less, like in the game's recipes.
Craftables.Tool.Tip: A tool is used, not consumed (a knife, a hammer, a station's tag).
Craftables.Levels.Note: Per level: what a player pays at each level of the recipe's skill (Engineering for buildings; an item recipe's own skill, such as Survival). Off, the higher levels pay less, as in the game's recipes.
Craftables.Levels.PerLevel.Tip: Set the amount for each skill level yourself (no skill, basic, medium, advanced, above advanced).
Craftables.Levels.Auto.Tip: What the game asks at each skill level, no skill first: the higher levels pay less, as in the game's recipes.
Craftables.Level.Tip: How many a player at this level of the recipe's skill pays (at least 1).
Craftables.Stock.Tip: Change how many materials the game's own recipes ask at each skill level.
Craftables.Stock.Title: Game recipes: materials per skill level
Craftables.Stock.Hint: Search a recipe of the game (CR_…), add it, then set what each skill level pays. The Craftables pak ships it for client and server.
Craftables.Stock.Warning: This replaces the game's own recipe: another mod that changes the same recipe conflicts with it (the pak loaded last wins). Export again after every game update.
Craftables.Stock.Search.Tip: Type at least 2 letters of a recipe name (CR_Improvised_Workbench, Bow …).
Craftables.Stock.Add.Tip: Override this recipe's amounts per skill level (starts from the game's own).
Craftables.Stock.None: No recipe of the game is overridden.
Craftables.Stock.Reset.Tip: Set every amount back to the game's own.
Craftables.Stock.Remove.Tip: Stop overriding this recipe: the game's own amounts apply again.
Craftables.Stock.Skill.Tip: The skill whose level picks the amount (the recipe's RelevantSkill).
Craftables.Stock.Game.Tip: The game's own amounts, no skill first.
Craftables.Stock.Changed: The game's recipe changed since these amounts were set (it now asks for {0}): they are not exported. Remove it and add it again.
Craftables.RemoveIngredient.Tip: Remove this ingredient from the recipe.
Craftables.Remove.Tip: Remove this craftable from the project (Undo brings it back).
Craftables.Import.Tip: Make a craftable from an FBX or OBJ file (a table, a weapon model, anything): Unreal Engine 4.27 imports and cooks it for SCUM, and the Craftables pak carries it. The first import compiles shaders and takes several minutes.
Craftables.Import.OtherProject: {0} was added to the project {1}, which was open when the import started.
Craftables.Import.NoEngine: Unreal Engine 4.27 was not found in {0}. Install it with the Epic Games Launcher, or set {1} to its folder.
Craftables.AddIngredient.Tip: Pick an item or an ingredient group from the 3D pictures and add it to the recipe.
Craftables.Picker.Title: Pick an ingredient
Craftables.Picker.Hint: Every item a player can carry, by category, and the ingredient groups of the game and of this project. Click one, set the amount, then Use.
Craftables.Picker.Search.Tip: Finds every inventory item of the game and of the mods the app reads, and every ingredient group (CI_), by name.
Craftables.Picker.Amount.Tip: How many without skill, 1 to 9999; skilled players need less, like in the game's recipes.
Craftables.Picker.Ok.Tip: Puts the picked item or group in the recipe.
Craftables.Picker.Cancel.Tip: Closes the picker; the recipe stays as it was.
Craftables.Ingredient.Change.Tip: Pick another item or group for this ingredient, from the 3D pictures.
Craftables.Ingredient.Badge.OwnTag.Tip: The game knows this item as {0}: the recipe asks for exactly this item.
Craftables.Ingredient.Badge.GroupOnly.Ti: This item has no tag of its own: the recipe asks for its group {0}, so any item of that group is accepted. Tick 'Only this item' to give it a tag of its own.
Craftables.Ingredient.Badge.NewTag.Tip: The export adds a new tag to this item's entity setup, a file of the game: the recipe then asks for exactly this item. Other mods that change the same item conflict with it. An item with uses or a stack (glue, a repair kit, arrows) counts by uses or pieces, as the game's own tags of such items do; any other item counts whole.
Craftables.Ingredient.Badge.NoTag.Tip: The game knows no tag for this item, so no recipe can ask for it yet: tick 'Only this item' to add one, or pick a group.
Craftables.Ingredient.Badge.Group.Tip: An ingredient tag of the game: every item that carries it is accepted.
Craftables.Ingredient.AddTag.Tip: Adds a new ingredient tag to the game's own entity setup of this item, so the recipe asks for exactly it. This changes a file of the game (only this item's, only when ticked); other mods that change the same item conflict with it. An item with uses or a stack (glue, a repair kit, arrows) then counts by uses or pieces, as the game's own tags of such items do; any other item counts whole.
Craftables.Use.Tip: Where it goes once made: built in the world, crafted into the bag, or both.
Craftables.Use.Build.Tip: Placed in the world like base building; its recipe is in the building menu.
Craftables.Use.Craft.Tip: Crafted into the bag like the game's items (items and power objects). An element is built; Both also crafts its item into the bag.
Craftables.Use.Both.Tip: Two recipes: one builds it, one crafts its item into the bag. Only for game elements that have an item (a workbench, a lamp); a bed has none.
Export.Module.Nothing: The {0} page has no changes to export yet.
Export.Module.EconomyWritten: EconomyOverride.json written (a server file, no pak).
Export.Module.NoServer: No server pak: set Settings → Server folder to build one too (a dedicated server cannot use the client pak).
Export.Module.ServerRefused: The server's {0} was NOT written: the package check refused it (see the report in the Server folder), and a server pak of an earlier export does not have these edits.
Export.Module.Needs: It uses what {0} adds: install that pak too.
Export.Module.Install: Copy the Client files into the game's Paks\~mods and the Server files into the server's mods folder; with two or more page paks, copy the Registry pak too. Restart the game, and restart the server with -fileopenlog (as for every mod pak).
Export.DecalsPendingDetail: {0}: the stickers drawn in the Decals tab are not in the pak (not applied, or changed since they were applied). Open Vehicles, the Decals tab, press Apply decals, then export again.
Export.Module.Button.Tip: Builds only this page's changes as a mod of its own: a client and a server pak, each with its .sig, plus the Registry pak that keeps the new assets of all your page paks known to the game. Export mod on the Map page builds the whole project in one pak instead.
Export.Module.MapOnly.Tip: Builds only the Map page's changes (levels, placed objects, holes) as a mod of its own, client and server, each with its .sig. Export builds the whole project in one pak.
Craftables.Steps.Intro: Go from step 1 to step 6. Hover any box or button for a short explanation.
Craftables.Steps.Note: Step 1: click «Add from the game» and pick an object in 3D (or import a 3D model). Then fill in the steps on the right and export in step 6.
Craftables.Step.Where: Where it shows up in the game
Craftables.Where.Build.Tip: Players place it in the world and build it with the ingredients, like walls and furniture: it is in the base building menu.
Craftables.Where.Craft.Tip: Players craft it into their bag in the crafting menu, like the game's items. Only items of the game and power objects can be crafted into the bag.
Craftables.Where.Both.Tip: Two recipes: built in the base building menu, and its item crafted in the crafting menu. Only for a copy of a game object that has an item (a workbench, a lamp; a bed has none).
Craftables.Where.InBuild: Players find it in the base BUILDING menu, section «{0}». They place it in the world and build it with the ingredients of step 3.
Craftables.Where.InCraft: Players find it in the CRAFTING menu, section «{0}». It is crafted into the bag with the ingredients of step 3.
Craftables.Where.AlsoCraft: Its item can also be crafted into the bag in the CRAFTING menu.
Craftables.WhatItIs.Tip: Furniture: a thing to place (chair, table). Station: other recipes can ask for it nearby, like a workbench. Power: makes electricity in a circle. Like the game's: a copy of the game's own object that keeps what it does (a bed you respawn at, a chest that stores).
Craftables.Step.Suggest.Tip: Replaces the ingredients with a recipe for the chosen material and the object's size, scaled from the game's own building recipes.
Craftables.Step.Files.Hint: The names of its files inside the mod and their folder. Keep them unless you need others: after the first export they stay fixed, because the game saves what players built by them.
Craftables.Step.Export.Hint: Builds the craftables as a mod of their own: a Client and a Server pak, each with its .sig, in the export folder of Settings. Copy the Client files into the game's Paks\~mods (every player) and the Server files into the server's mods folder. Export mod on the Map page builds the whole project instead.
Craftables.More.Tip: Rarely needed: the station players must stand next to, electricity, and the values of a copied game object (health, decay, limits).
Craftables.KindChange.Warning: If this craftable was exported, objects players already placed keep their saved class: after the next export they behave as the new kind (a bed made furniture is no longer a respawn point).
Craftables.Building.LikeGame: This is the game's {0}: build it like the game's, with its own placement, health, decay and repair.
Craftables.Building.LikeGame.Tip: Makes it a clone of the game element's own family (Element). Its asset names stay, so what players already built behaves like the game's element after the next export.
Craftables.Building.Borrowed: The game ships no recipe for {0}: a copy of the Large Log Shed's recipe builds it (your ingredients, section and picture), with its placement check drawn in to the middle so the ghost can turn green with you standing inside it. The element, its health, decay and repair are the game's.
Craftables.Building.Borrowed.Tip: The recipe only decides the crafting menu, the ingredients and the skill; what is built is the game's element.
Craftables.Building.NeedsFlag.Tip: Checked: players can build it only inside a flag area (base territory). Unchecked: anywhere. Written as _canBePlacedWithoutFlag on every level of its element.
Craftables.Building.RepairCost.Tip: 100 = the game's. One use of a repair tool restores the element's HealthRepairedPerUse × 100 ÷ this, so the uses a repair takes follow the damage: 200 % takes twice as many, 50 % half. What one use consumes is the repair tool's data (the same for every element), not the recipe's materials.
Craftables.Building.Large: Placed like the game's large buildings, with the Large Log Shed's recipe: on the highest ground under it, upright, turned only around its vertical axis. Its placement check is drawn in to 1.5 m around its middle, so the ghost can turn green with you standing inside it; what is built keeps its full collision.
Craftables.Building.LargeStation: Placed like the game's large buildings, keeping the workbench's recipe (it stays a station): on the highest ground under it, upright, turned only around its vertical axis. Its placement check is drawn in to 1.5 m around its middle, so the ghost can turn green with you standing inside it; what is built keeps its full collision.
Craftables.Building.Large.Tip: For furniture and stations of 3 m and more. The game centres the ghost on the point you aim at, 2-3 m ahead, so inside a big building its floor meets your feet and the ghost stays red (Overlapping character). The game shrinks what is checked for its own wall lamps and workbench; this does the same for the building.
Craftables.Building.InFront.Tip: Experimental, for mid-sized furniture only. Its recipe gets a PlacementLocationOffset that moves the placement point. Tested in 3.5.0: the game adds it in world directions after finding the ground, so the ghost can float and does not turn with you. Big buildings get a drawn-in placement check instead and do not need it.
Craftables.Building.InFront.Meters.Tip: How far ahead it is placed (experimental). Automatic: 0 below 3 m, else half its size + 1 m, at most 15 m (the 15 m cabin: 8.5 m). Change it if it should come closer or go farther.
Craftables.Building.InFront.Axis.Tip: Experimental. The game's data suggests +X is straight ahead of you. If the ghost appears beside or behind you, pick the direction that puts it in front and export again.
Craftables.Building.Placement: Without "Place in front", where the ghost appears and Shift + mouse wheel are the game's code: the game centres the ghost on the point you aim at.
Craftables.Building.Placement.Tip: None of the game's 333 base elements stores a mesh offset; the game's own cabins are centred the same way. "Place in front" moves the placement point in the recipe instead (experimental).
Craftables.Element.Title: Element values
Craftables.Element.Levels.Tip: The game's own upgrade chain of this element, cloned whole; each level has its own values. Adding or removing levels is not in this version.
Craftables.Element.Inherited: Kept from the game's parent class: {0}
Craftables.Element.Inherited.Tip: This level does not store these values: it keeps the ones of its parent class, which this version cannot change.
Craftables.Element.Respawn.Tip: It keeps the game bed's respawn flag (_isUsedForRespawn); respawning at a crafted bed is not yet tried in game. Respawn delay and price are the server's settings (ServerSettings.ini / the game's RespawnSettings: shelter cooldown, initial time and price), not a value of the bed.
Craftables.Element.Health.Tip: Hit points of the placed element (_healthPoints): higher lasts longer.
Craftables.Element.HoursToDecay.Tip: Hours until it decays inside a flag area (_hoursToDecay).
Craftables.Element.HoursToDecayOutsideFl: Hours until it decays outside any flag area (_hoursToDecayOutsideFlagArea).
Craftables.Element.CanBeDamaged.Tip: Off: weapons and tools cannot damage it (_canBeDamaged).
Craftables.Element.PlaceWithoutFlag.Tip: Can be placed outside a flag area (_canBePlacedWithoutFlag).
Craftables.Element.PlaceInBuilding.Tip: Can be placed inside the map's buildings (_canBePlacedInBuilding).
Craftables.Element.PlaceInRestrictedArea: Can be placed where building is restricted (_canBePlacedInRestrictedArea).
Can stand on other base elements, like a floor or a table (_canBePlacedOnOtherBaseElements).
Craftables.Element.MaxPerFlagArea.Tip: How many can stand in one flag area (_maxInstancesPerFlagArea).
Craftables.Element.MaxPerSquad.Tip: How many one squad can have (_maxInstancesPerSquad).
Map.MyModels.Title: My models
Map.MyModels.Hint: Your own 3D models (FBX or OBJ), imported once and kept in the project; the Craftables page lists the same ones. Place one, then move, turn and scale it like any object. Players collide with it as the import made it: they can walk on it and into it. Export mod carries the model into the pak with the placement.
Map.MyModels.None: No models yet: import one here or on the Craftables page.
Map.MyModels.Place.Tip: Puts this model where the camera aims and records it in the project (Ctrl+Z undoes).
Map.MyModels.Import.Tip: Pick an FBX or OBJ file: Unreal Engine 4.27 imports it and cooks it for SCUM, and it joins My models here and on the Craftables page. The first import compiles shaders and takes several minutes.
Map.MyModels.Imported: {0} is in My models of the project {1}: Place puts it where the camera aims.
Map.MyModels.Gone: The model {0} cannot be placed ({1}). Import it again.
Assets.MakeCraftable.Tip: Add this mesh or Blueprint to the project's craftables (Craftables page) with a suggested recipe.
Projects.ExportCraftables: Also build the Craftables mod (its own pak, when the project has craftables)
Projects.ExportCraftables.Tip: pakchunk<N+1>-<Name>Craftables_P.pak next to the project's pak, with a copied stock .sig; its AssetRegistry keeps the project's records. Unticked, the export removes the Craftables pak an earlier export left there.

Map.Companions.Rule.OwnEffect: its own fire, light or sound
Map.Companions.Rule.WaterTwin: the other side of the water
Map.Companions.NoteSpawned: Items already spawned and fires players lit stay on a running server: they are in its save. An item spawner's items: Clean saved items.
Map.Companions.NoteClassEffect: Some effects come from the object's class, not from this placement: they go only with the whole object.
Map.Companions.NoteShared: Greyed rows stand nearer to another object and stay with it; tick one to delete it anyway.
Map.Companions.BatchTitle: Delete {0} and {1} things that belong to it
Map.Companions.Deleted: Deleted {0} and {1} things that belong to it
Map.Companions.Looking: Looking for what belongs to the deleted objects...

Map.Companions.Tip.OnlyThis: Delete only the object you picked; its fire, light and sound stay (Shift+Delete does the same)
Map.Companions.Tip.WholeObject: Delete the whole object this part belongs to, with the effects its class adds
Map.Companions.Tip.Row: Ticked rows are deleted with the object; a locked row goes with it in any case
Settings.DeleteWithCompanions.Tip: On: deleting an object also deletes its fire, light, smoke and sound at the spot and the actors attached to it, after a short list to check. Off, or Shift+Delete: only the object.
Map.Companions.Kept: Kept, because other parts hang under them: {0}
Map.CopyRefused.OtherLevel: {0} is not pasted into another level: its brush shape ({1}) holds data the studio cannot carry into another level yet. Duplicate it inside its own level instead.

Map.ItemSpawner.Placed: {0} is placed as an item spawner. The game saves every item it spawns: deleting or undoing the spawner later does not take items it already spawned out of a world. Map → Clean saved items removes them from the save (server or single player).
Map.ItemSpawner.Deleted: {0} is an item spawner. Items it already spawned stay in servers' and single player saves: the mod cannot remove them. After the export, Map → Clean saved items removes them from the save.
Export.ServerNoStub: The server pak would carry {0} sound event(s) cooked for players (e.g. {1}), and the dedicated server crashes on those ("Serial size mismatch"). Export.StaleServerPak: Removed the old server pak(s) {0}: this export built no matching server pak, and a server pak from an earlier export no longer matches the new client pak.
Export.StaleServerCopy: The server's mods folder still holds {0} from an earlier export, and this export built no server pak: it no longer matches the new client pak. Build the server pak too, or remove that file from the server.

Export.OtherModeRemoved: Removed {0} from the server's mods folder: the whole-project paks of a project and its page paks must never be installed together.
Export.ModOutdated: An imported mod is out of date
Export.RefusedDetail: {1} was NOT written: the package check found {0} problem(s) that could crash the game or the server. A pak left in the folder by an earlier export does not have these edits. Report: {2}
Export.ServerRefused: Server pak NOT exported (the client pak is ready)
Export.Parity: Every player needs {0} in the game's Paks\~mods; the server needs {1} in its mods folder. Restart the game and the server after copying.
Export.ParityClientOnly: Every player needs {0} in the game's Paks\~mods. A server with this mod needs the server pak of the same export too: set Settings → Server folder and export again.
Export.ParityServerRefused: Every player needs {0} in the game's Paks\~mods. The server's {1} was NOT written: the package check refused it, and a server pak of an earlier export does not have these edits. Fix the problems and export again before a server runs this mod.

Map.DragCancelled: Move cancelled (Esc): the object is back where it was
Map.View.Tip: Look along an axis, around the selection or the ground in the middle of the view. Numpad: 7 top, 1 front, 3 right, Ctrl for the other side, 9 the opposite side, . frame the selection
Map.View.Opposite.Tip: The same view from the other side (Numpad 9)

Map.Wireframe.Tip: Draw the scene as the edges of its triangles (F3 or Shift+Z). The sky, the grid and the gizmo stay as they are, and a click still picks what is drawn.

Map.Levels.ShowSelected.Tip: Load exactly the levels chosen in the tree (Ctrl+click adds one, Shift+click a range; they also load by themselves after a short pause). Nothing else streams in around them; Isolate hides the island's terrain too.
Map.Levels.TooMany.Message: {0} levels are selected; the first {1} are loaded.

Map.SavedItems.Choose.Tip: Single player: %LOCALAPPDATA%\SCUM\Saved\SaveFiles\SCUM.db. Server: SCUM\Saved\SaveFiles\SCUM.db in the server's folder. The game and the server must be closed.
Map.SavedItems.UseArea.Tip: Also lists, within this many metres of the object selected on the Map, items of the same kinds that no spawner owns (moved items, or spawners the project cannot place any more).
Map.SavedItems.Find.Tip: Lists the saved items of this project's removed or reverted item spawners. It only reads the save.
Map.SavedItems.Remove.Tip: Copies the save to SCUM.db.studio-backup-<date> next to it, then removes the ticked items (and what is stored inside them) from the save.
Map.SavedItems.Restore.Tip: Puts the newest backup made here back in place of the save.
Map.SavedItems.Ready: Ready: Find lists what this project's removed item spawners left in this save.
Map.SavedItems.Found: {0} saved item(s) belong to removed item spawners. Untick any you want to keep, then Remove ticked.
Map.SavedItems.None: No saved item belongs to this project's removed item spawners.
Map.SavedItems.NoTargets: This project never removed or reverted an item spawner: nothing to look for.
Map.SavedItems.NoSelection: Select an object on the Map first: the area is around it.
Map.SavedItems.Removed: Removed {0} item(s) and {1} stored inside them. Backup: {2}. Start the server or the game again.
Map.SavedItems.Busy.Running: {0} is running: quit the game and stop the server, then try again.

Map.SavedItems.Failed: The save could not be read or changed: {0}

Map.Guards.Title: Robot out, NPC area in
Map.Guards.Hint: SCUM has no NPC that stands guard or walks a route: armed NPCs come from the game's encounters, which bring them near players and take them away again. This removes the robot and makes its route an NPC area: NPC spawn posts along it, in a sub-zone of the place's threat zone that spawns only the chosen NPCs.
Map.Guards.Type.Tip: Which armed NPCs the area spawns: an NPC encounter of the game (guards or drifters and their level). The area gets its own copy of zone settings that use it, with every other encounter at 0 and one encounter at a time, like the game's own NPC areas.
Map.Guards.Posts.Tip: How many spawn posts along each robot's route, spread evenly from the spawner to its last patrol point. The NPCs spawn at some of them, never one on each; how many come is the encounter's own.
Map.Guards.WholePlace.Tip: On: every sentry robot of this level is replaced in one step. Off: only the selected one.
Map.Guards.Warnings.Tip: Read before replacing: what changes, and what only the game can confirm.
Map.Guards.Warn.Removed: • The robot is removed; its place's guarded zone forgets it.
Map.Guards.Warn.NoRoute: • Never one NPC standing on each post. 1 to 3 NPCs come only while a player walks into the area, 30 to 200 m ahead of them and out of their view; then the area rests 20 to 30 minutes.
Map.Guards.Warn.Zone: • The NPC area is a sub-zone of the place's own threat zone, the way the game makes its NPC areas; its settings are its own copy, so no other zone changes. Where no threat zone covers the posts, it is a zone of its own.
Map.Guards.Warn.Count: • The NPCs leave soon after the players do. A character under new-player protection (its first 2 hours on a server) gets none. They may bring zombies along.
Map.Guards.Warn.Game: • Only the game shows whether they come here. Test on a local server with a character older than 2 hours: walk towards the posts from about 150 m away, at walking pace, looking ahead.

Craftables.Groups.Hint: A group is a new ingredient tag (CI_Group_ + its name). Every item you put in it gets that tag in this mod, so a recipe of this project that asks for the group accepts any of those items. To do that, the export changes each item's entity setup, a file of the game (also for an item of the game's own): the changed setups go into the Craftables pak, every player and the server need that pak, and another mod that changes the same items conflicts with it. When every item of a group has uses or is a stack (glue, a repair kit, arrows), the amount counts uses or pieces; otherwise it counts whole items. DLC items cannot join a group. Only groups a recipe asks for are exported.
