Guide.WindowTitle: Installing UE4SS on a cloud server
Guide.Title: Installing UE4SS on a cloud (rented) server
Guide.Intro: UE4SS lets Lua mods run inside your SCUM Dedicated Server. On a rented server the app cannot reach the files, so you put them there yourself (about 10 minutes). Use it only on a server that is yours.
Guide.Warning: UE4SS runs code inside the server process: a faulty mod can crash the server. Keep a copy of the server folder before you start. Some hosts do not allow extra DLL files or a server without BattlEye: ask your host first.
Guide.S1.X: You need: file access to the server (FTP/SFTP or the panel's file manager), the right to upload a .dll file into the game's folder, and a way to start the server without BattlEye (the launch parameter -nobattleye or a BattlEye switch in the panel). SCUM Server is a Windows program; if your host runs it under Linux, see the note under step 4.
Guide.S2.X: Open github.com/UE4SS-RE/RE-UE4SS/releases, the release named experimental-latest, and download the file UE4SS_v3.0.1-….zip (about 9 MB). Take the standard one, not the one that starts with zDEV.
Guide.S3.X: Unpack the zip. You get the file dwmapi.dll and the folder ue4ss.
Guide.S4.T: Upload the files to the server
Guide.S4.X: Open the server's folder SCUM\Binaries\Win64 (the one with SCUMServer.exe) with FTP/SFTP or the file manager. Upload dwmapi.dll and the whole ue4ss folder there, so that dwmapi.dll lies next to SCUMServer.exe.
Guide.S4.Wine: Linux/Wine host: the host must start the server with the environment variable WINEDLLOVERRIDES="dwmapi=n,b", otherwise Wine ignores dwmapi.dll. Ask your host to set it.
Guide.S5.X: Open ue4ss/UE4SS-settings.ini on the server and set these lines (leave the rest as it is):
Guide.S5.After: Without the second line the server freezes soon after it starts. This is what the Install UE4SS button does on a local server. With UE4SS's stock hooks the server crashes as soon as a player joins, so every hook except HookEngineTick and HookUObjectProcessEvent is set to 0.
Guide.S6.X: Open ue4ss/Mods/mods.txt and put 0 after the stock mods (CheatManagerEnablerMod, ConsoleCommandsMod, ConsoleEnablerMod, SplitScreenMod, LineTraceMod, BPML_GenericFunctions, BPModLoaderMod). Keep the line Keybinds : 1 last. Do the same in mods.json ("mod_enabled": false).
Guide.S7.X: In the host's panel add the launch parameter -nobattleye (or switch BattlEye off). A server that runs UE4SS must start without BattlEye.
Guide.S8.X: Upload the mod's folder ue4ss/Mods/<ModName> (it holds Scripts/main.lua) and add the line <ModName> : 1 to ue4ss/Mods/mods.txt and the entry to mods.json. You can make the mod on your own computer: install UE4SS into a copy of the server folder, use this app's Server page, then upload the folder it made.
Guide.S9.X: Restart the server from the panel. When it is up, open ue4ss/UE4SS.log: a line Starting Lua mod '<ModName>' means the mod loaded. A new mod loads when the server starts.
Guide.S10.X: The server does not start or freezes: delete dwmapi.dll (the server then runs without UE4SS) and read ue4ss/UE4SS.log, where a mod that did not load shows its error. After a SCUM update, function names can change: take the class list again with the Class and function list mod.
Guide.Copy.Tip: Copy the settings lines of step 5 to the clipboard.
Lua.Open.Tip: Opens the Lua editor in its own window: a catalog of the functions and events a server mod can use, with notes on what worked on a real server, and a place to write the script.
Lua.Tab.Catalog.Tip: Functions, events, rules and ready pieces that were tried on a real server.
Lua.Tab.Game.Tip: Every function the server's class dump lists (thousands). Names only: they exist, but nobody has to have tried them.
Lua.Search.Tip: Type words of a name or of a description; all of them must match.
Lua.Group.Tip: Show only one group of the catalog.
Lua.Legend: ✔ tried on the server   ○ exists, effect not tried   ✖ does not work or crashes
Lua.List.Tip: Pick an entry to read what it does and to insert its example.
Lua.Status.Seen: Exists in the game, effect not tried to the end
Lua.Status.Unsafe: Does not work or crashes the server
Lua.Game.Search.Tip: Type words of a class or function name, like HUD or Quest. At most 300 are shown.
Lua.Game.Hook.Tip: Puts a RegisterHook on the picked function into the script. The arguments differ per function: look them up before using them.
Lua.Game.List.Tip: The functions of the server's class dump.
Lua.Game.NoDump: No class dump yet. Switch the ScumStudioDump mod on once while the server is empty; it writes ue4ss\scum_dump.txt.
Lua.Game.Count: {0} functions in the server's class dump.
Lua.Mods.Tip: The Lua mods already on the server. Picking one loads its script here.
Lua.Name: Mod name
Lua.Name.Tip: The folder of the mod on the server: letters, digits, _ and - (at most 40).
Lua.New.Tip: Starts an empty script under the name in the box.
Lua.Check.Tip: Looks for syntax errors, for game functions that do not exist in the class dump and for mistakes that hurt the server before.
Lua.Save.Tip: Checks the script, writes it to the server's mods folder and switches the mod on. A running mod reloads by itself; a new one needs one server restart.
Lua.Code.Hint: Write the script here, or insert pieces from the catalog.
Lua.Findings.Tip: What the check found. A cross is an error that stops saving; an exclamation mark is a warning.
Lua.Insert.Tip: Puts the example at the caret in the script.
Lua.Finding.UnknownFunction: The game has no function {0} (not in the class dump).
Lua.Finding.FormatInteger: %d fails on the game's fractional numbers: use %.0f or math.floor.
Lua.Finding.SoftPointer: Writing {0} (a soft class pointer) crashed the server before: only read or copy it.
Lua.Finding.HideChat: Message:set does not hide a chat line: everybody still sees it.
Lua.Finding.LoopOutsideGameThread: FindAllOf in a loop without ExecuteInGameThread: the game may be touched only from the game thread.
Lua.Finding.PlayerInHook: A player is used inside a hook with no ExecuteWithDelay: this crashed the server before. Answer 1 s later.
Lua.Check.Ok: No problems found; every game function exists in the class dump.
Lua.Check.OkNoDump: No problems found. The game functions were not checked: there is no class dump yet.
Lua.NotSaved: Not saved: fix the errors first.
Lua.Saved: Saved to {0}. A running server reloads a changed mod by itself; a new mod needs one restart.
Loot.Open.Tip: Opens the loot editor in its own window: loot groups and chances for the searchable containers of a place (a dungeon), written as the server's own loot customization.
Loot.NoDefaults: The game's loot presets are not exported yet. Type this command once in the game chat (you must be an admin), then reopen this window:
Loot.Zones.Tip: The zones that already have changed loot on the server. Picking one loads its rectangle and its changed presets.
Loot.ZoneName.Tip: The zone's folder name under Loot\Spawners\Presets\Override: letters, digits, _ and - (at most 40).
Loot.Corner.Tip: A corner of the zone's rectangle on the map (UE cm). Any two opposite corners; the file gets them in the order the game wants.
Loot.GuardSet.Tip: A guard set of the open project: the zone can cover its posts, which is handy for a dungeon.
Loot.Margin.Tip: How far outside the posts the zone reaches (cm).
Loot.FromGuards.Tip: Sets the rectangle from the picked guard set's posts plus the margin.
Loot.Changed.Tip: The presets whose loot is changed inside the zone. Pick one to edit it. Everywhere else the game's own loot stays.
Loot.RemovePreset.Tip: Deletes the picked changed preset from the server: the game's own loot applies in the zone again.
Loot.RemoveZone.Tip: Deletes the zone folder with every changed preset in it from the server.
Loot.GamePresets.Tip: Every loot preset the game has (its path with dashes). A searchable object uses one of them, for example a crate pile uses Street-Military-Examine_Crate.
Loot.Search.Tip: Type words of a preset name, like Crate or Military.
Loot.AddPreset.Tip: Starts a changed copy of the picked game preset in this zone. It begins with the zone rules off and a chance of 100%, so the container is never empty.
Loot.Save.Tip: Checks the preset and writes it, with the zone's rectangle, into the server's loot customization folder.
Loot.Chance.Tip: The chance that one search gives anything. Leave empty to keep the preset's own (9 for a crate pile). 100 for a container that always gives something.
Loot.QuantityMin.Tip: The fewest items one search gives.
Loot.QuantityMax.Tip: The most items one search gives. 1 to 3 means one to three items, picked from the groups below.
Loot.FilterZone.Tip: On: items the game allows only in some kinds of place (coast, mountain ...) are filtered. Keep it off in a dungeon outside the game's own zones, or nothing drops.
Loot.LocationChance.Tip: On: the place's own chance modifier multiplies the chance. Keep it off in a dungeon outside the game's own zones.
Loot.LocationDamage.Tip: On: the place's own wear modifier changes how worn the items are.
Loot.Duplicates.Tip: On: the same item may drop twice in one search.
Loot.Groups.Tip: What a search can give. Each search picks items from the groups, the more common a group the more often.
Loot.AddGroup.Tip: Adds an empty loot group to the preset.
Loot.Rarity.Tip: The group's rarity, its weight against the other groups: Abundant 32, Common 16, Uncommon 8, Rare 4, Very Rare 2, Extremely Rare 1.
Loot.Weight.Tip: How much more often this group is picked than an Extremely Rare one.
Loot.Entries.Tip: One entry per line: a loot tree tag (ItemLootTreeNodes.Military.Weapons.Rifles, a whole group or one item) or an item id (KeyCard). Pick tags from the tree on the right.
Loot.Hint: A container is any searchable object of the game, for example a crate pile placed on the map. Its preset is changed only inside the zone.
Loot.AfterSave: After saving, type this in the game chat so the server reads it (no restart needed):
Loot.LoadTree.Tip: Reads the tags and items of the game's loot tree from the opened game files, so they can be searched and added.
Loot.TagSearch.Tip: Type words of a tag, like Rifles or Flares.
Loot.AddTag.Tip: Adds the picked tag to the picked loot group.
Loot.TagList.Tip: Tags of the loot tree: a group (Military.Weapons) or one item.
Loot.NoGuards: Pick a guard set that has posts (and a number for the margin) first.
Loot.ZoneTaken: The rectangle covers the posts of {0}.
Loot.Added: {0} is now changed in this zone.
Loot.PickGroupAndTag: Pick a loot group and a tag first.
Loot.NoGameFiles: Open the game files first (Settings) to read the loot tree.
Loot.Saved: Saved to {0}. Now type {1} in the game chat.
Loot.Problem.NoLoot: The preset gives nothing: add a loot group with an entry.
Loot.Problem.Entry: '{0}' is not a loot tree tag (ItemLootTreeNodes....) or an item id.
Loot.Problem.Quantity: The counts {0} do not fit: the most must not be below the fewest.
Loot.Problem.Probability: '{0}' is not a chance between 0 and 100.
